fields.label: Filled up Form
fields.field_information: Medical Services Data Upload Guidance This section is dedicated to uploading the completed Medical Services Data Form. This form captures critical operational metrics, including patient load, available medical facilities, and overall hospital performance. Data Scope: The form must be populated with historical statistics spanning the past 3 years. Authorized Personnel: To ensure data accuracy, it is highly recommended that this form be completed by a physician, medical officer, or a relevant healthcare administrator at the facility. Template Access: If you do not have the form, you can download the blank template from the Office Order section on top menu bar or directly via clicking the link below. . Download Form .

fields.label: Number of Beds of Existing Hospital Building
Soil Test Report (click i button for detail)
fields.field_information:
Soil Test Report Guidance

Please upload the soil test report using the following prioritized hierarchy:

1. Primary Option: Existing soil test reports from nearby buildings, or assessed Standard Penetration Test (SPT) values for the area with soil profile.

2. Secondary Option: A minimum of three (3) SPT values covering a significant portion of the hospital building footprint and adjacent areas with soil profile.

3. Final Option: Commission a new, comprehensive soil test with soil profile. Note: This should only be pursued if options 1 and 2 are entirely unavailable.

Accepted Uploads: Managed, assumed, or formally tested soil report documentation.

fields.label: As Built Arc Drawing of Existing Hospital Building (Floor Plans)
fields.field_information:
📋 Floor Plan Submission Guide

To help us accurately assess the building layout, please upload the official floor plan of the existing hospital building.

Can't find the official copy? A clear CAD drawing or a hand-drawn sketch with accurate dimensions works perfectly too! Please ensure your plan includes these key features:

1. Room & Space Labels: Clearly identify the functionality of each room, including stairs, lift cores, voids, wash blocks, and toilets.

2. Ramp Locations: Mark the existing ramp, or indicate where a future ramp could be built if one isn't currently present.

3. Setback Distances: Show the clearance and setback dimensions all around the main hospital building.

4. Key Elevations: Include the Floor height, Plinth height, and Finished Ground Level (FGL) measured with respect to the adjacent road.

Thank you for taking the time to provide these details!

fields.label: Plinth Area of Existing Hospital Bldg (sqft)
Master Plan of Campus (Demarking Visually Vulnerable Buildings)
fields.field_information:
💡 Master Plan Checklist

To ensure your master plan is complete and passes review smoothly, please make sure your drawing clearly includes the following major campus components and nearby features:

1. Building Functions: A detailed note on how each building is used (especially if the name doesn't make it obvious).

2. Safety & Vulnerability: Clearly marked structures or buildings on the UHC campus that are visually vulnerable or structurally weak.

3. Boundary Demarcation: The master plan will cover total land area (acres), land ownership status, site boundary line, mouza map etc.

4. Water & Drainage: The location of the nearest freshwater sources and the main water/waste disposal points.

5. Road Accessibility: The exact widths of the main road and all approach roads leading to the existing hospital building.

6. Building Clearances: Accurate setback distances measured all around the main hospital building.

fields.label: Visual Evidence of the area (Image or video)
fields.field_information:
📸 Site Media & Context Guide

Visuals tell the story best! Please upload quality images or a short video clip of the area to help the team make informed decisions.

What to capture:

1. Important landmarks, unique structures, or defining features of the site.

2. Critical areas that need immediate engineering decisions or attention.

3. For main Hospital building: Elevations, Ward Interior, OPD, Emergency, OT, Labor Room other indoor facility and spaces.

4. Short voice narratives or text notes pointing out key details as you record.

⏱️ Upload Tip: To ensure a fast and smooth upload process, please keep video clips as short and focused as possible!

fields.field_information:
ℹ️ Foundation Design Capacity

Please enter the total number of floors for which the building's foundation was originally designed, regardless of how many stories are currently built.

Example: For a "5-Storied Building with a 10-Storied Foundation", you should enter 10.

fields.label: Structural Condition of Main Hospital Bldg (Describe)
fields.field_information:
Structural Condition Guidance

Please provide a detailed assessment of the building's structural state to help determine if it should be repaired, retrofitted, or demolished. Your description must highlight:

Structural Integrity: Document the location and severity of visible cracks (in columns, beams, or load-bearing walls), concrete spalling, exposed rebar, or structural sagging.

Deformation & Distress: Note any tilting, foundation settlement, or severe vulnerability that threatens overall stability.

Drainage & Core Damage: Identify active water logging, deep dampness, or leaks that may have weakened the internal concrete or reinforcement over time. presence of lime terracing or any other facility in roof.

Feasibility Assessment: Based on your visual inspection, state whether the damage appears localized (reparable), system-wide but salvageable (retrofittable), or critically compromised (requiring demolition).
.
